# postcard-serializable

Postcard is not self-describing, so some Rust types compile, serialize and then
cannot be read back. A `serde_json::Value` encodes without complaint and fails
to decode, because decoding it needs `deserialize_any`, which postcard does not
have. A `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "...")]` field leaves out bytes the
decoder still expects, so everything after it reads wrong. You find out at
runtime, and if the bytes were written by another machine or an older build,
you find out late.

This derive moves that failure to compile time.

```toml
[dependencies]
postcard-serializable = "0.1"
postcard-serializable-types = "0.1"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
```

```rust
use postcard_serializable::PostcardSerializable;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Default, Serialize, Deserialize, PostcardSerializable)]
struct Event {
    id: u64,
    name: Option<String>,
    payload: Vec<u8>,
}
```

Put `postcard_serializable_types::PostcardSerializable` on whatever sends bytes,
and a type nobody checked cannot reach it:

```rust
use postcard_serializable_types::PostcardSerializable as Checked;

fn send<T: Checked>(value: &T) -> postcard::Result<Vec<u8>> {
    postcard::to_allocvec(value)
}
```

## What it refuses

- A field of type `serde_json::Value` or `Box<dyn Trait>`.
- `skip_serializing_if`, `skip_serializing`, `skip_deserializing` and `flatten`
  on a type or a field.
- A field whose type has not opted in. Every field has to implement the trait,
  so the check follows your types all the way down. `#[serde(skip)]` is allowed,
  because a field skipped both ways never reaches the wire.

The standard integer, float, string and collection types are already in, along
with tuples up to four, `Option`, `Box`, `Uuid`, `Duration` and `PathBuf`.

## What it does not do

It reads attributes and type names, and asks the compiler whether each field
implements a marker trait. It does not prove anything about a hand-written
`Serialize` impl, and `impl PostcardSerializable for MyType {}` is a promise
nobody checks. It catches the mistakes people actually make, not every mistake
there is.

It is also narrower than it should be. The trait requires `Default`, so a type
without one cannot use it. `uuid` is a required dependency. You have to depend
on two crates where one should do. All three can change before 1.0, and pinning
is reasonable until then.
